findings.evidence: Basic.lean:112-113 `/-- A projection `ψbar_±` of the antiquark field. -/ | antiquark (p : QuarkProjection)`; roadmap MultiPartonCorrelations/README.md:412 `ψ̄_+ γ^+ ψ_+`, :374-375 "each a quark field with a chirality and a good/bad label"; EpsilonEridani/Particles/Parton/GPD/Basic.lean:73 `AntiquarkForwardLimitToPdfAtScale` uses antiquark for f̄.
findings.fix: Rename the constructor to `quarkBar` (or `conjQuark`) and follow through on `massDimension_antiquark`, `lightConeSpin_antiquark_good/bad`, `twist_antiquark_good/bad`, `quarkNumber_antiquark`; say "conjugate quark field ψ̄" in the docstrings.
findings.issue: Constructor `antiquark (p : QuarkProjection)` and its docstring ("A projection `ψbar_±` of the antiquark field", line 112; same wording line 20, 44, 108) call ψ̄ the antiquark field. ψ̄ is the Dirac-conjugate quark field; the roadmap §0.2 writes `ψ̄_+ γ^+ ψ_+` and describes the data as "a quark field with a chirality and a good/bad label", with no antiquark field. The repo uses "antiquark" in its standard sense for the antiquark density elsewhere, so the term is now overloaded.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:101-102 `/-- The purely transverse component `F^{ij}` … -/ | transverse` vs Basic.lean:97-98 `/-- The components `F^{+i}` … -/ | plusTransverse` and Basic.lean:405-406 "`F^{+i} F^{+j}` in transverse field strengths"; roadmap Suggested.lean:39 names `F^{+i}` `transverseStrength`.
findings.fix: Rename the constructor to `purelyTransverse` (matching its own docstring "The purely transverse component `F^{ij}`") and update the derived lemma names, or reserve "transverse field strength" in the prose for `F^{ij}` only.
findings.issue: `FieldStrengthComponent.transverse` denotes `F^{ij}`, but the file's own docstrings use "transverse field strength" for `F^{+i}` (`plusTransverse`): lines 68-69, 405-406 ("`F^{+i} F^{+j}` in transverse field strengths") and 420-421. The bare name therefore means the opposite of the surrounding prose, and `twist_transverse`/`lightConeSpin_transverse` inherit the ambiguity.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:158-159 `massDimension_fieldStrength (c : FieldStrengthComponent)` vs :191 `@[simp] theorem twist_transverse : (fieldStrength .transverse).twist = 2`; naming conventions: "`_`-separated strings in a lemma name correspond to a definition name or connective".
findings.issue: The field-strength simp lemmas omit the `fieldStrength` constructor from their names — `lightConeSpin_plusTransverse` (169), `lightConeSpin_plusMinus` (172), `lightConeSpin_transverse` (174), `lightConeSpin_minusTransverse` (176), `twist_plusTransverse` (187), `twist_plusMinus` (189), `twist_transverse` (191), `twist_minusTransverse` (193) — although the subject term is `LightConeField.fieldStrength .plusTransverse` etc. The quark lemmas spell out both constructors (`lightConeSpin_quark_good`, `twist_quark_bad`) and `massDimension_fieldStrength` uses the constructor, so the names are inconsistent and unguessable; `plusMinus`/`transverse` are constructors of `FieldStrengthComponent`, not of `LightConeField`.

summary: Three naming defects: `antiquark` is nonstandard terminology for the conjugate field ψ̄ and clashes with the repo's existing use of the word; `FieldStrengthComponent.transverse` names F^{ij} while the file's own prose calls F^{+i} transverse; and the field-strength lemma names omit the `fieldStrength` constructor that the sibling quark and massDimension lemmas carry.
